findings.failure_mode: SSRF from /preview reaches localhost-only admin service and triggers backup wipe
findings.trigger: An attacker sends GET /preview?url=http://127.0.0.1:9000/wipe-backups to the public service. public.py fetches that URL server-side; internal_admin.py executes wipe_backups() and deletes /var/backups/shop, returning 'done', which is echoed back in the preview response (confirming success).
findings.evidence:
public.py:9-11 `url = request.args["url"]
    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
    return resp.text[:2000]`
findings.business_impact: Unauthenticated remote destruction of all shop backups (/var/backups/shop) by any party who can reach the public /preview endpoint, causing permanent data loss and loss of recoverability after any incident.
findings.blast_radius: Components on the path: public.py, internal_admin.py
attack_chain: public.py:9-11 - The /preview route takes the attacker-supplied 'url' query parameter with no validation, allowlist, or scheme/host restriction, and passes it directly to requests.get().

internal_admin.py:9-12 - The outbound request from public.py can target 127.0.0.1:9000, the loopback-only admin service. Its /wipe-backups route performs a destructive shutil.rmtree with no authentication, token, or source check — it relies solely on network locality for protection, which the SSRF in public.py bypasses.

Fails here: internal_admin.py assumes 'listening on 127.0.0.1' is an access control, but public.py performs server-side requests to arbitrary URLs, so any host that can reach /preview can make the server itself call the loopback admin endpoint. There is no validation of the url parameter (scheme, host, IP range) in public.py and no authentication on /wipe-backups.
